definitions.explanation: Describes movement or action that is frustratingly slow or sluggish.

examples.japanese: {渋滞|じゅうたい}で{車|くるま}がのろのろ{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: The cars are moving slowly due to traffic.

examples.japanese: のろのろ{歩|ある}いていたら{遅刻|ちこく}するよ。
examples.english: If you walk so slowly, you'll be late.

examples.japanese: {前|まえ}の{車|くるま}がのろのろ{走|はし}っていて、なかなか{進|すす}めなかった。
examples.english: The car in front was going so slowly that I couldn't make any progress.

notes:
のろのろ is a mimetic word ({擬態語|ぎたいご}) expressing frustratingly slow movement. Unlike ゆっくり, it always carries a negative connotation — implying that the slowness is annoying or problematic.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- のろのろ{運転|うんてん}: slow driving
- のろのろ{進|すす}む: to inch forward (e.g., in traffic)
- のろのろ{歩|ある}く: to walk sluggishly
- のろのろする: to dawdle, be sluggish

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ゆっくり: slowly (neutral — can be positive: "take your time")
- のろのろ: slowly (negative — frustratingly slow)
- もたもた: slow and clumsy (implies fumbling or incompetence)
- ぐずぐず: dawdling (implies indecision or procrastination)
- とろとろ: sluggish (gentler; also means thick/gooey for food)
